# `dataset.metadata`

[dataset](README.md) · metadata

CLOSED v0.1.15. It was an open object — `additionalProperties` unset and `properties` empty — so it accepted any key, and that is the hatch `status: draft` and `confidence: I` came through while the column object beside it was strictly closed. `table` REMOVED 2026-10-05: it duplicated `table.name` in 16 of 16 descriptors, and the FILENAME too — a triple. It had zero readers (the one hit was a writer), and the filename<->table.name link is already enforced by tools/check_relation_identity.py, so the fact was policed twice over without this third copy.

> **2 keys at this level carry no description in `mac.schema.json`.** The place to fix one is the schema, which is its one home; this page is generated and cannot hold the answer.

### `kind`

*string* · optional · 2 legal values

WHICH OF THE TWO HOMES THIS DESCRIPTOR DESCRIBES — the raw schema-of-record under `data/sources/`, or the served relation under `data/datasets/`. They are ONE shape: identical `table.*` and `columns[].*`, so this key is the whole difference. It was `{type: string}` with no enum and no description until 2026-10-05, which made the single discriminator of the data plane an open field. `external: true` sat beside it as a second marker and is removed: the generator could only ever emit it inside `if not served`, so it was present-or-absent typed as a boolean, it was read by nothing, and it said what this key already says.

Legal values:

- `raw_source`
- `served_dataset`

### `status`

*string* · optional · 2 legal values

A LIFECYCLE FACT ABOUT THE FILE, NOT A GRADE OF THE MEASUREMENT. `retired` is read by check_datasets_are_grounded, which skips a descriptor whose relation is gone — the one real consumer. `draft` is NOT permitted: a measurement is not a draft, it either happened or it did not, and every generated descriptor was born `draft` for no reader at all.

Legal values:

- `measured`
- `retired`
